stem: Which is the best example of inclusive-growth evaluation?

options.C: District-disaggregated learning, health and quality-job outcomes

option_audit.A: Incorrect: announced infrastructure alone is not evidence of realized human-development outcomes or inclusion.
option_audit.B: Incorrect: aggregate growth alone cannot establish how benefits or capabilities are distributed; UNDP explicitly distinguishes human development from economic growth alone.
option_audit.C: Best answer: geographically disaggregated education, health and employment-quality outcomes better test inclusion; NITI monitors SDGs at sub-national level. Caveat: neither cited source prescribes this exact three-item composite or a particular job-quality metric.
option_audit.D: Incorrect: project outlay is a financing input, not measured outcomes or distribution.

sources.finding: UNDP identifies health, knowledge and standard of living, explicitly warning against using growth alone; HDI by itself does not capture inequality.
NITI monitors SDGs at national and sub-national levels and emphasizes localization and leaving no one behind.
IHDI and other measures address inequalities and deprivations omitted by headline HDI.

limitations: The phrase quality-job outcomes is a reasonable evaluation component but not separately established as a mandatory measure by these sources.
No district-level dataset was calculated or verified.
This is an original practice question, not an authenticated official PYQ.
Author-side bounded evidence only; no independent reviewer, PDF change or R1-R8 promotion.
